tagline: Building a better world through engineering and project management
hero_kpi_rationale: The backlog is a key indicator of the company's financial health and its ability to generate long-term revenue. It represents contracts already awarded and in execution, providing visibility into future cash flows.

kpis.name: Backlog
kpis.explanation: Total expected revenue from contracts already awarded
kpis.description: FLR's backlog decreased in 2025 due to an execution pace exceeding new award activity. The backlog consists of 81% reimbursable contracts.

kpis.name: New Awards
kpis.explanation: Total value of new contracts awarded
kpis.description: FLR's new awards declined by 21% in 2025 to $12.0 billion, primarily due to lower demand in the Energy Solutions division and customer slowdowns amid budgetary pressures.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.description: FLR's revenue decreased by 5% in 2025 to $15.5 billion, impacted by a $643 million revenue reversal related to the Santos project ruling in Australia, partially offset by growth in the Urban Solutions and Mission Solutions divisions.

kpis.name: Segment Profit
kpis.explanation: Operating profit generated by the three business segments (Urban Solutions, Energy Solutions, Mission Solutions)
kpis.description: FLR's total segment profit was -$109 million in 2025, reflecting losses in the Energy Solutions division (-$414 million) due to cost overruns on three infrastructure projects, partially offset by gains in Urban Solutions and Mission Solutions.

kpis.name: General and Administrative Expenses
kpis.description: FLR's general and administrative expenses remained stable at $196 million in 2025, demonstrating financial discipline and cost control at the corporate level.
kpis.signal: Stability in general and administrative expenses in 2025

kpis.name: Backlog 2025
kpis.explanation: Total expected revenue from contracts already awarded in 2025
kpis.description: FLR's backlog declined by 10% in 2025 to $25.5 billion due to an execution pace exceeding new award activity. 81% of the backlog consists of reimbursable contracts.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total revenue of 15.503 Bn$ for last fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of -0.051 Bn$ for last fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.description: Operating income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Operating income of -0.378 Bn$ for last fiscal year (FY2025).

risks.title: Market cyclicality
risks.score_rationale: FLR's revenues and profits depend heavily on new contract awards, exposing the company to economic cycles and demand fluctuations in the sectors it serves.

risks.title: Operational and contract risks
risks.score_rationale: Fixed-price contracts carry risks related to delays and cost overruns that are not fully recoverable. In 2025, FLR recorded significant cost overruns on three infrastructure projects.

risks.title: Dependence on skilled workforce
risks.score_rationale: FLR's ability to operate profitably depends strongly on its ability to hire and retain qualified personnel, which is challenging due to competition for talent in the industry.

risks.title: Customer credit risks
risks.score_rationale: FLR is exposed to credit risks related to customer payment delays or defaults. In 2025, significant payment delays impacted the Mexican joint venture's operations.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks
risks.score_rationale: FLR operates in foreign countries (40% of backlog is international) and is exposed to political, regulatory, and economic risks. Customers are slowing commitments due to macroeconomic uncertainties.

risks.title: Litigation and regulatory risks
risks.score_rationale: FLR faces complex litigation (Santos ruling of $643 million in 2025) and multiple regulatory risks across its global operations.

risks.title: Divestiture integration and execution
risks.score_rationale: FLR is finalizing its divestitures (Stork, NuScale, China fabrication) which require complex operational management and could impact cash flows and operations.

ai_positioning.summary: FLR is gradually integrating artificial intelligence and related technologies into its project management operations. The company emphasizes using AI and technology to improve cost and schedule performance to support project quality and client outcomes.
evidence: Foster a high-performance culture of project delivery by using A.I. and technology to improve cost and schedule
